issues.legal_issue: A summary public-revenue recovery procedure that creates no new substantive right cannot be used to recover a claim that was time-barred when recovery was initiated.
material_facts: The proceedings sought recovery of loans made by banks for agricultural purposes and by a financial corporation, under a law extended to those debts for speedy recovery.
The recovery law provided a method of recovery but did not create a new right to payment.
The statutory scheme allowed a person who paid under protest to seek a refund, and the creditor initiated recovery by a written requisition.
The issue was whether claims already barred by limitation when the requisition was issued could be recovered through that procedure.
issues.conclusion: A claim that was time-barred when the creditor issued the recovery requisition was not an amount legally recoverable through the statutory procedure and could not be recovered under it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court interpreted Sections 69(2), 70 and 71 of the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968. A procedure for speedy recovery does not enlarge the creditor’s substantive claim or remove a debtor’s limitation defence unless the law expressly provides for that result. The Court relied on Hansraj Gupta v. Dehra Dun-Mussoorie Electric Tramway Co. Ltd. (AIR 1933 PC 63), which treated ‘money due’ under a special recovery procedure as excluding time-barred claims; New Delhi Municipal Committee v. Kalu Ram (1976 (3) SCC 407), which held that a recovery provision covered only arrears not otherwise time-barred; and The Director of Industries, U.P. v. Deep Chand Agarwal (AIR 1980 SC 801), concerning the speedy-recovery purpose of such procedures. It distinguished Khadi Gram Udyog Trust v. Ram Chandraji Virajman Mandir (1978 (1) SCC 44), which concerned a tenant’s statutory opportunity to avoid eviction, and noted that although limitation ordinarily bars the remedy rather than extinguishing the debt, coercive statutory recovery does not thereby become available for a time-barred claim.

predicates.recovery_through_summary_public_revenue_: A creditor sought to recover a debt through a summary public-revenue recovery proceeding.
predicates.claim_time_barred_when_recovery_initiate: The creditor’s claim was barred by limitation when the recovery process was initiated.
predicates.recovery_procedure_does_not_create_new_s: The recovery procedure provided a method of collection but did not create a new substantive right to recover the debt.

issues.definition: When a creditor uses a summary public-revenue recovery proceeding for a claim already barred by limitation, and the procedure only changes the method of collection, the claim cannot be recovered through that procedure.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory restriction on suits concerning execution, discharge or satisfaction of a recovery demand does not bar a separate suit expressly available to a person who paid the demand under protest, including a suit raising limitation.
material_facts: The statutory scheme allowed a person facing recovery to pay under protest and provided for an enquiry into the protest.
It expressly allowed the person who paid under protest to sue for a refund of all or part of the payment.
A separate provision directed that certain disputes between the recovery authorities and the defaulter be determined under the recovery law rather than by suit.
The Court considered whether that restriction displaced the expressly provided refund suit and the debtor’s ability to raise limitation in it.
issues.conclusion: The restriction on suits did not cover the expressly preserved refund suit; a person who paid under protest could sue for a refund and argue that the recovered claim was time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 70(1)–(3) and 72 of the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968, the right to sue for a refund after payment under protest is distinct from disputes concerning execution, discharge or satisfaction of a written demand. Section 72 does not displace the suit expressly preserved by Section 70(3). The Court also relied on the statutory scheme to conclude that the debtor’s limitation defence remained available in that suit.

predicates.recovery_under_public_revenue_procedure: A creditor pursued recovery of a debt under a public-revenue recovery procedure.
predicates.debtor_paid_under_protest: The debtor paid the amount claimed while formally protesting the recovery.
predicates.statute_expressly_preserves_refund_suit: The governing law expressly allows a person who paid under protest to bring a suit for a refund.

issues.definition: When a debtor pays under protest in a public-revenue recovery proceeding and the governing law preserves a refund suit, the debtor may bring that suit and raise limitation as a defence.
